claims.text: E9: 12+ Antigravity Nidhoggr sessions stalled on 'Allow using this MCP tool? hfo/board_status', active session shows 'Waiting for user input..' blocked at FIRST tool use
The scheduler is NOT the defect on Antigravity. Tasks fired on cadence correctly. The break is after wake, at authorization.
A permission-stalled session is byte-identical to a session that never fired: no rows, no error, no exit code. Strongest confirmation of negative-evidence blindness (H_new) in the analysis.

RETRODICTION: E9 explains world-state capsule gaps G2 (local_4f13b00b) and G3 (local_35e95836), both recorded as 'nothing on disk, session still RUNNING'. 'Still RUNNING' is how a permission-stalled session presents.

claims.text: REFRAME: the 'both timeout' diagnosis in all 3 hourly SKILL.md may be a misattributed permission stall. 'Timeout' is what a stall looks like from inside an agent that cannot see the dialog.

new_failure_classes_proposed.definition: A loop wakes on cadence but cannot complete without synchronous human authorization, so scheduled execution degrades to a queue of nudges. Fire != completion.

naming_pushback: Operator proposed L_SCHEDULER_FIRES_PERMISSION_STALLS as one entry. Recommend AGAINST a single L_-prefixed name, per R13: L_ denotes a behavioral refusal (something an agent must decline to do) and nothing here is agent misbehavior - the agent obeyed and waited. Collapsing an incident class and a behavioral vector into one name is the same ontology collision that produced the 6-vs-19 failure-class incident. Two names, two registries, one pointer.
